w: Once one of Germany's most important Benedictine houses, Hirsau Abbey drove the 11th and 12th century Cluniac reform movement so thoroughly that German history calls it the Hirsau Reforms. French troops wrecked the complex in 1692; nobody rebuilt it, and locals later quarried the ruins for stone.
s: The abbey that gave Germany its own Reform movement
_facts: once one of Germany's most important Benedictine abbeys

w: The Emperor's Chair: a compact range of volcanic hills topping out at 556.6 metres, standing apart from the Black Forest proper on the floor of the Upper Rhine Plain. Its volcanic soil leaves some of the region's warmest vineyard slopes, spread across Emmendingen and Breisgau-Hochschwarzwald.
s: A volcano's hills called the Emperor's Chair
_facts: volcanic hill range, maximum height 556.6m
name means Emperor's Chair

w: A glacial lake shaped by moraines the Feldberg glacier dropped behind it in the last Ice Age, now 1.3 square kilometres of water averaging 20 metres deep. Its outflow, the River Gutach, joins the Haslach to form the Wutach on its way to the Rhine. The spa town on its shore shares its name.
s: The glacial lake that named its own spa town
_facts: 1.3 sq km lake, average depth 20m
formed by moraines of the Feldberg glacier
outflow is the River Gutach, feeding the Wutach toward the Rhine
spa town of the same name sits on its north shore

w: Southeast of the Titisee, in the same Breisgau-Hochschwarzwald district, the Schluchsee is a reservoir rather than a natural lake, a dammed stretch of water standing in for what was once just a valley. It sits close enough to Freiburg im Breisgau for an easy day trip.
s: The Black Forest's other lake, dammed not natural
_facts: a reservoir lake, not a natural lake
sits southeast of the Titisee in the Breisgau-Hochschwarzwald district

w: Its name means look-into-the-country, and for centuries before that it went by Erzkasten, the ore box, for the silver dug from its slopes. First recorded as Schouwesland in 1347, the 1,284-metre mountain sits about 10km southeast of Freiburg's centre, now drawing day-trippers instead of miners.
s: The ore box that became a lookout
_facts: 1,284m mountain; name means look-into-the-country
about 10km southeast of Freiburg im Breisgau's centre

w: Opened only in 2014, the Black Forest's national park splits into two blocks about 3.5km apart: 7,615 hectares around Ruhestein and 2,447 more around Hoher Ochsenkopf and Plattig, strung along the main ridge of the Northern Black Forest. It protects the wildest ground in a range long managed for timber.
s: The Black Forest's youngest wild ground, split in two
